examples.en: Please feel free to state your opinion in the meeting.

examples.ko: 그는 정책에 대한 반대 의견을 당당히 개진했어요.
examples.en: He confidently voiced his opposing view on the policy.

examples.ko: 의견을 개진하기 전에 근거부터 정리해 두세요.
examples.en: Before you state your opinion, organize your evidence first.

examples.ko: 신입 사원도 눈치 보지 않고 생각을 개진할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even new employees can voice their thoughts without worrying about others' reactions.

examples.ko: 주민들이 시청에 불만을 개진한 뒤 길이 고쳐졌어요.
examples.en: After residents voiced their complaints to city hall, the road was repaired.

examples.ko: 자기 입장만 개진하고 남의 말은 안 들으면 대화가 안 돼요.
examples.en: If you only state your own position and don't listen to others, there is no conversation.

explain: '말하다'보다 훨씬 딱딱해서 회의, 토론, 공문서 같은 격식 있는 자리에서 어울려요. 보통 '의견', '주장', '입장', '불만'과 함께 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '의견을 내다'나 '말씀드리다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is much stiffer than '말하다' and suits formal settings such as meetings, debates and official documents. It usually goes with words like '의견', '주장', '입장' and '불만'. In everyday conversation, '의견을 내다' or '말씀드리다' sounds more natural.

en: be supported (receive support from evidence); be backed up

examples.en: This claim is backed up by solid data.
That theory was supported by several experiments.
If skill doesn't back it up, confidence alone is not enough.

examples.ko: 말이 행동으로 뒷받침돼야 믿을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Words can be trusted only when actions back them up.
There is not a single piece of supporting evidence.

examples.ko: 이 계획은 충분한 예산으로 뒷받침될 거예요.
examples.en: This plan will be backed by a sufficient budget.

explain: '뒷받침하다'는 받쳐 주는 쪽이고, '뒷받침되다'는 받쳐 줌을 받는 쪽이에요. 보통 '자료, 증거, 실력으로 뒷받침되다'처럼 주장이나 계획이 주어로 와요.
explain_en: '뒷받침하다' is the side that gives support, and '뒷받침되다' is the side that receives it. The subject is usually a claim or plan, as in '자료로 뒷받침되다' (backed up by data).

examples.ko: 계약하기 전에 내용을 면밀하게 확인해야 해요.
examples.en: You need to check the details carefully before signing a contract.

examples.ko: 경찰이 사고 원인을 면밀히 조사하고 있어요.
examples.en: The police are carefully investigating the cause of the accident.

examples.ko: 계획이 면밀하지 않으면 중간에 문제가 생겨요.
examples.en: If the plan isn't thorough, problems arise midway.

examples.ko: 면밀한 검토 끝에 이번 안을 결정했어요.
examples.en: After careful review, we decided on this proposal.

examples.ko: 부장님은 일 처리가 면밀해서 실수가 거의 없어요.
examples.en: Our manager is meticulous in handling work, so there are hardly any mistakes.

examples.ko: 면밀했던 준비 덕분에 발표가 잘 끝났어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the thorough preparation, the presentation went well.

explain: '꼼꼼하다'와 비슷하지만 조사, 검토, 분석, 계획처럼 일의 과정에 격식 있게 써요. 사람의 성격을 가볍게 말할 때는 '꼼꼼하다'가 자연스러워요. 부사는 '면밀히', '면밀하게' 둘 다 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is similar to '꼼꼼하다' but is used more formally for work processes like investigation, review, analysis and planning. To casually describe a person's character, '꼼꼼하다' sounds more natural. The adverb can be either '면밀히' or '면밀하게'.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 어려도 명민해서 금방 이해해요.
examples.en: Even though that child is young, they're sharp and understand quickly.

examples.ko: 명민한 판단 덕분에 큰 손해를 피했어요.
examples.en: Thanks to a sharp judgment, we avoided a big loss.

examples.ko: 새로 온 직원이 일을 명민하게 처리해서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was surprised that the new employee handled the work so astutely.
That student's eyes look bright and sharp.

examples.ko: 그 판사는 명민하고 공정한 사람으로 알려져 있어요.
examples.en: That judge is known as a sharp and fair person.

examples.ko: 명민하지 않았다면 그 위기를 넘기기 어려웠을 거예요.
examples.en: If he hadn't been so sharp, it would have been hard to get through that crisis.

explain: 머리 회전이 빠르고 판단이 정확하다는 뜻이라, 사람뿐 아니라 판단이나 눈빛에도 써요. 말할 때는 '똑똑하다'가 가장 흔하고, 명민하다는 글이나 격식 있는 말에 어울려요. 비슷한 '영민하다'도 있어요.
explain_en: It describes quick thinking and accurate judgment, and applies to people as well as to judgments or the look in someone's eyes. In speech '똑똑하다' is the usual choice, while 명민하다 suits writing and formal talk. There is also a similar word, '영민하다'.

examples.en: That boss was incompetent and ruined the company.
I'm hopeless at cooking.
It is hard to work under an incompetent leader.
Sometimes I feel that I am incompetent.
There was criticism that the government was incompetent.

examples.ko: 무능하게 보일까 봐 질문을 못 했어요.
examples.en: I couldn't ask a question for fear of looking incompetent.

explain: 무능하다의 반대말은 '유능하다'예요. 사람에게 쓰면 강한 비난이라서 부드럽게 말할 때는 '서툴다'나 '못하다'를 써요. '요리에는 무능해요'처럼 자기 자신에게 농담으로 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: The opposite of 무능하다 is 유능하다. Said about another person it is a strong accusation, so to soften it people use 서툴다 or 못하다. People also use it jokingly about themselves, as in 요리에는 무능해요.

examples.en: The company takes customer opinions into account.
The teacher incorporated the question into the class.

examples.ko: 우리는 내일 새 의견을 반영할 거예요.
examples.en: We will incorporate the new opinions tomorrow.
It takes time to incorporate opinions.
A painting reflects the look of its era.
I sent the file with the corrections applied.

explain: 의견이나 요청을 실제 결과에 넣는다는 점이 '듣다'와 달라요. '의견을 반영해 주세요'처럼 부탁할 때도 자주 써요. 작품이나 말이 사회와 시대를 그대로 비춰 보여 줄 때도 써서 '시대를 반영하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Unlike '듣다' (listen), it means actually putting opinions or requests into the result, and you can ask '의견을 반영해 주세요'. It is also used when a work or statement mirrors a society or era, as in '시대를 반영하다'.

examples.ko: 이 단어는 속된 표현이라 발표에서는 안 써요.
examples.en: This word is vulgar, so I don't use it in presentations.

examples.ko: 너무 속되게 들릴까 봐 다른 표현으로 바꿨어요.
examples.en: I changed it to another expression because it might sound too crude.

examples.ko: 속되지 않은 말로 바꿔서 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Please rephrase it in less vulgar words.

examples.ko: 그 표현은 친구끼리 쓰기에도 조금 속돼요.
examples.en: That expression is a bit crude even to use among friends.

examples.ko: 속되다고 생각하는 사람도 있지만 저는 재미있어요.
examples.en: Some people think it's vulgar, but I find it fun.

examples.ko: 말투가 너무 속돼서 면접에서는 고치는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: Your way of speaking is too crude, so fix it for the interview.

explain: '속된 말', '속된 표현'처럼 말에 가장 많이 써요. 이런 말을 가리키는 명사는 '속어'예요. 욕만 뜻하는 게 아니라 격식 있는 자리에 안 맞는 거친 말투도 포함돼요.
explain_en: It is most often used for language, as in '속된 말' and '속된 표현'. The noun for such words is '속어'. It doesn't mean only swearing, but also rough wording that doesn't suit formal situations.

en: prioritize; give priority to; put first

examples.en: I put my family first above all.
The company decided to put safety first.

examples.ko: 일을 우선시하다 보니 친구를 못 만났어요.
examples.en: Because I prioritized work, I couldn't see my friends.
The teacher is someone who puts students' opinions first.
Let's decide first what to prioritize.
He prioritized health over money.

explain: 어떤 것을 먼저 챙기거나 더 중요하게 여길 때 써요. '○○을/를 우선시하다'로 쓰고, 뒤에 '△△보다'를 붙여 비교하기도 해요. '우선하다'는 '○○이/가 우선하다'처럼 주어가 앞서는 것이라 문장 구조가 달라요.
explain_en: 우선시하다 is used as ○○을/를 우선시하다 and is often followed by a comparison with △△보다. 우선하다 differs in sentence structure: the thing that comes first becomes the subject, as in ○○이/가 우선하다.

dis.h: put something first as a priority

p.n: 우선하다 is mostly 'take precedence'; with a person doing the prioritizing 우선시하다 is the natural choice.

en: selection of a right person; choice of a right person

examples.ko: 새 대표의 인선이 다음 주에 발표돼요.
examples.en: The selection of the new CEO will be announced next week.

examples.ko: 이번 인선은 결과를 보고 평가해야 해요.
examples.en: This choice of person should be judged by the results.
Opinions were divided over who to pick for the committee.

examples.ko: 인선에 시간이 오래 걸려서 일정이 미뤄졌어요.
examples.en: The selection took a long time, so the schedule was pushed back.

examples.ko: 후임 인선 작업이 아직 끝나지 않았어요.
examples.en: The work of choosing a successor is not finished yet.

examples.ko: 인선 기준을 먼저 정하는 게 좋겠어요.
examples.en: It would be better to set the selection criteria first.

explain: 장관, 대표, 위원처럼 중요한 자리에 알맞은 사람을 골라 정하는 일이라서 뉴스에서 주로 나와요. 일반 직원을 뽑을 때는 '채용'이나 '선발'을 써요. '후임 인선', '인선 작업'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is about choosing a suitable person for an important post such as a minister, head or committee member, so it mostly appears in the news. For hiring ordinary staff, use '채용' or '선발'. It is common in phrases like '후임 인선' and '인선 작업'.

en: select a right person; choose a right person

examples.en: The president selected a new minister.
You must be fair when choosing committee members.
The head decided to pick the team leader personally.
No one has been chosen as the successor yet.

examples.ko: 후임을 인선하는 데 한 달이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a month to choose the successor.
Since the pick was made carefully, I'm looking forward to the results.

explain: 목적어로는 장관, 대표, 위원 같은 높은 자리를 맡을 사람이나 그 자리가 와요. '발탁하다'와 비슷하지만 인선은 적임자를 가려 정한다는 점이 중심이에요. '인선을 하다'처럼 명사로 풀어 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: Its object is the person for a high post such as a minister, head or committee member, or the post itself. It is close to '발탁하다', but the focus is on picking the right person for the job. You can also say '인선을 하다' using the noun.

examples.en: This time the ad strategy really paid off.
My friend's advice worked, so I passed the interview.

examples.ko: 일찍 출발한 것이 주효할 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think leaving early will pay off.

examples.ko: 가격을 낮춘 전략이 주효했는지 손님이 늘었어요.
examples.en: Maybe lowering the price worked, because there are more customers.

examples.ko: 공부 계획을 세운 방법은 별로 주효하지 않았어요.
examples.en: Making a study plan that way did not work very well.
Did the new study method work?

explain: '효과가 있다'와 같은 뜻이지만 훨씬 격식 있는 말이라 뉴스, 기사, 발표에서 많이 나와요. 보통 '주효했다'처럼 과거형으로 어떤 방법이나 전략이 좋은 결과를 만들었을 때 써요. 친구와 이야기할 때는 '통했다', '먹혔다'를 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It means the same as '효과가 있다' (to be effective) but is much more formal, so it appears often in news, articles and presentations. It is usually used in the past tense, '주효했다', when a method or strategy produced a good result. In casual talk people more often say '통했다' or '먹혔다'.

examples.en: He is an employee who is dedicated to his work.
This book has very solid content.
It's a drama made faithfully to the original.
If you stick to the basics, your skills improve.
He's a loyal and sincere friend, so I trust him.
I made a plan to spend the day fully.

explain: '성실하다'는 꾸준히 열심히 하는 태도를, '충실하다'는 맡은 일, 규칙, 원작에 어긋나지 않고 제대로 따르는 모습이나 내용이 알차다는 말이에요. 보통 '~에 충실하다'로 써요. 책이나 식사, 하루가 알찰 때도 쓸 수 있지만 이때는 '알차다'를 더 많이 말해요.
explain_en: 성실하다 is about a steady, hardworking attitude; 충실하다 means sticking faithfully to a duty, rule or original, or having rich content. The usual pattern is ~에 충실하다. It also works for a book, meal or day being full, though 알차다 is more common for that.

examples.en: Communication is the most important thing in a team.

examples.ko: 대화가 적어서 팀 커뮤니케이션을 늘리기로 했어요.
examples.en: We talk little, so we decided to increase team communication.
They hire people with good communication skills.
I take a communication class.
Foreign languages are a big help for communication.
People communicate not only with words but also with facial expressions.

explain: 커뮤니케이션은 회사나 학교 이야기에 자주 나오는 외래어이고, 같은 뜻으로 '소통'도 써요. '커뮤니케이션을 하다', '커뮤니케이션이 되다', '커뮤니케이션이 잘 안 되다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: 커뮤니케이션 is a loanword that often appears in talk about work or school, and '소통' can be used for the same idea. Typical uses are '커뮤니케이션을 하다', '커뮤니케이션이 되다' and '커뮤니케이션이 잘 안 되다'.
